## Gateway replay parity

Each prompt of the test split (100 prompts) is sent through the gateway once for every offline decision about it, and the model that served it is compared with the one the trainer chose: 700 requests.

| Strategy | Requests | Agreeing | Agreement | Deterministic | Errors | Accuracy | Total cost | Cost per success |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| latency | 100 | 97 | 0.970 | no | 2 | 0.600 | $1.5000 | $0.0250 |
| strongest | 100 | 100 | 1.000 | yes | 0 | 0.750 | $3.0000 | $0.0400 |
| cheapest | 100 | 100 | 1.000 | yes | 0 | 0.500 | $0.5000 | $0.0100 |
| static | 100 | 100 | 1.000 | yes | 0 | 0.600 | $1.2000 | $0.0200 |
| quality/strict | 100 | 100 | 1.000 | yes | 0 | 0.800 | $4.0000 | $0.0500 |
| quality/balanced | 100 | 100 | 1.000 | yes | 0 | 0.750 | $3.0000 | $0.0400 |
| quality/economy | 100 | 100 | 1.000 | yes | 0 | 0.650 | $1.3000 | $0.0200 |

- Deterministic agreement: 1.000 (threshold 0.999 for every deterministic strategy)
- Overall agreement: 0.996
- Parity: pass

The gateway's latency strategy adapts its estimates to observed attempts; the offline latency router uses the SIMULATED priors only, so its agreement is reported but not part of the parity check.

## Gateway load

Each scenario runs against a gateway started for it. Overhead is the end-to-end time of a request less the time of its provider attempts, as the stored decision records it, queueing included. Decision time is the time routing took.

### load-zero

Providers answer at once.

| Scenario | Requests | Throughput (req/s) | Latency p50 (ms) | Latency p95 (ms) | Latency p99 (ms) | Overhead p95 (ms) | Decision p95 (us) | Error rate | RSS max (MiB) | CPU mean (%, proc_stat_interval) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open_loop_50rps | 750 | 49.5 | 1.50 | 3.25 | 4.50 | 0.75 | 120 | 0.000 | 50.0 | 12.5 |
| closed_loop_c16 | 3000 | 495.0 | 30.50 | 44.25 | 51.50 | 2.50 | 150 | 0.010 | 100.0 | 85.5 |

CPU method `proc_stat_interval`: the mean of the CPU time the gateway process used between consecutive samples (utime and stime from /proc/<pid>/stat), as a percentage of one CPU.

### load-profiled

Providers take the time of the simulated latency profiles.

| Scenario | Requests | Throughput (req/s) | Latency p50 (ms) | Latency p95 (ms) | Latency p99 (ms) | Overhead p95 (ms) | Decision p95 (us) | Error rate | RSS max (MiB) | CPU mean (%, ps_lifetime_average) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open_loop_200rps | 3000 | 199.5 | 100.50 | 250.25 | 400.75 | 12.50 | 180 | 0.000 | 75.0 | 30.5 |
| closed_loop_c1 | 3000 | 1.5 | 600.25 | 900.50 | 1200.75 | 1.25 | 90 | 0.000 | 30.0 | 2.5 |

CPU method `ps_lifetime_average`: the mean of the ps pcpu readings, each the CPU time of the gateway process over its whole life so far and not over the last sampling interval, as a percentage of one CPU.

p95 gateway overhead < 20 ms: pass (12.50 ms, profiled open loop 200 rps)

## Fault injection

The providers fail, time out, cut streams short and leave usage out. The accounting invariants are checked on the books the gateway reports after the traffic.

| Tenant | Requests | Streaming | Success rate | Partial streams | Retries | Failovers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bench | 2000 | 1000 | 0.950 | 12 | 80 | 60 |
| bench-over | 200 | 100 | 0.750 | 5 | 10 | 0 |

| Invariant | Status | Books |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a. Spend equals the sum of usage records | holds | bench: spent $0.0400 (40000000 nano-USD), usage $0.0400 (40000000 nano-USD); bench-over: spent $0.0065 (6500000 nano-USD), usage $0.0065 (6500000 nano-USD) |
| b. Reservations return to zero | holds | bench: reserved $0.0000 (0 nano-USD); bench-over: reserved $0.0000 (0 nano-USD) |
| c. Spend stays within budget (bench) | holds | spent $0.0400 (40000000 nano-USD), budget $1.0000 (1000000000 nano-USD) |
| d. Overshoot equals spend beyond budget (bench-over) | holds | overshoot $0.0035 (3500000 nano-USD), spent $0.0065 (6500000 nano-USD), budget $0.0030 (3000000 nano-USD) |
| d. Overshoot is positive (bench-over) | holds | overshoot $0.0035 (3500000 nano-USD) |

Accounting invariants: holds

## Reproduce

Run from the repository root. The offline numbers come from the trainer and the gateway numbers from the benchmark driver. The last command regenerates this file and the results block of the README.

```sh
make data
make train
make evaluate
make bench-replay RUN_ID=golden-run
make bench-load RUN_ID=golden-run
make bench-faults RUN_ID=golden-run
make report RUN_ID=golden-run
```
